sections.heading: ProduceBlockV4 with Bid (beacon-APIs#627)
sections.summary: No consensus to merge the PR now; discussion to continue async with a goal of inclusion by Hoodi.
sections.body:
- Luca (Vero) presented [beacon-APIs#627](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/627), which extends the existing `produceBlockV4` endpoint so a validator client can fetch bids directly from builders and supply a chosen bid to connected Beacon nodes for block production.
  - Primary motivation: multi-Beacon-node setups benefit from deduplicating builder requests and centralizing bid monitoring in the VC rather than tracking each BN independently.
  - Existing precedent: some node operators already use Vouch in a similar pattern where the VC contacts builders.
- Potuz (Prysm) raised concerns that this is a significant change, making the VC more fragile, and questioned why the same benefit couldn't be achieved by designating a single Beacon node to contact builders with a failover BN.
  - Luca argued that VC-level failover is simpler because multi-BN validator clients query all connected BNs simultaneously, and a shared slashing protection database can allow multiple VC instances.
- Potuz acknowledged there's nothing fundamentally wrong with allowing a user-provided bid on the BN side and that off-protocol markets it might enable cannot be prevented anyway.
- Nico Flaig (Lodestar) reported he has the endpoint fully implemented and tested end-to-end, but raised three technical concerns:
  - Payload attributes are emitted in the previous slot based on a prediction; the bid Vero fetches may be incompatible with the proposer head computed at slot start.
  - Vero calls `produceBlockV4` later in the slot due to builder timing games; Lodestar currently does not optimize for late-slot API calls.
  - The change adds 2–3 new branches in the `produceBlock` API code path.
- If the BN rejects the provided bid (incompatible with proposer head, invalid, etc.), the design falls back to a peer-to-peer bid or local block building—bid inclusion is "best effort."
- Miguel Tenorio noted that if this use case is not standardized, operators may build custom proxies between BN and VC, which is worse.
- Decision deferred: Jihoon concluded there is not enough consensus to merge. Luca will create a discussion thread; the target is to finalize by Hoodi.
- Luca confirmed the endpoint has been tested on devnet-8 for several weeks.

sections.heading: Builder Exit and Missed Slots — Consensus Specs PRs 5694 vs 5695
sections.summary: Agreement to merge Nico's PR (consensus-specs#5695) for reordering requests when a builder exits and slots are missed.
sections.body:
- Two competing consensus-specs PRs address the edge case where a builder wins a bid, exits, and at least one epoch of slots is missed:
  - [consensus-specs#5694](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5694): drafts the payment to the proposer of the last block before the missed-slots gap (Potuz's approach).
  - [consensus-specs#5695](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5695): reorders requests to handle the edge case (Nico's approach), considered a less breaking change.
- Jihoon noted that 5695 had gathered more client support and proposed merging it.
- Potuz stated he is not fully happy with 5695 but would be more unhappy if no decision is made; he could not find an attack vector after spending time trying. He noted 5694 is simpler but accepted 5695.
- Potuz confirmed that Lighthouse's Michael had explicitly stated he prefers Nico's PR (5695).
- Pawan (Lighthouse) confirmed he would review and approve; after hearing Michael's preference, agreed to proceed.
- Agreement: Jihoon will work on merging consensus-specs#5695.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Beacon API PRs
sections.summary: Six Glamsterdam-related beacon-APIs PRs need client reviews; Lighthouse and Teku will review, aiming to merge before Sepolia fork.
sections.body:
- Barnabas flagged six open Beacon API PRs, all Glamsterdam-related:
  - [beacon-APIs#638](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/638)
  - [beacon-APIs#641](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/641)
  - [beacon-APIs#655](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/655)
  - [beacon-APIs#657](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/657)
  - [beacon-APIs#659](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/659)
  - [beacon-APIs#615](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/615)
- Nico (Lodestar) confirmed he has approved all of them and has implementations in Lodestar; described them as trivial compared to the bid endpoint.
- Pawan (Lighthouse) committed to reviewing and commenting today.
- Enrico (Teku) said he had only reviewed the last one previously but will review the rest and report back.
- Barnabas asked to aim for merging before the Sepolia fork (Tuesday) and having implementations ready for Hoodi.
- Nico confirmed the plan is to have everything sorted for Hoodi so users can rely on the endpoints.

sections.heading: CL Spec Release and Test Coverage for Request Reordering
sections.summary: No new spec release needed immediately; Nico's PR includes a regression test that catches the reordering change.
sections.body:
- Barnabas asked whether a new CL spec release is needed; Potuz initially said yes for the request-ordering change.
- Nico clarified that implementing the reordering today still passes all current beta-2 spec test vectors—no existing test covers the edge case.
  - However, consensus-specs#5695 includes a new test that will fail if a client does not implement the reordering.
- Potuz expressed concern about forking Hoodi with a consensus-breaking change that existing released tests do not cover, but accepted the situation and said he would open the Prysm implementation PR immediately.
- Enrico (Teku) confirmed the new test in the PR is sufficient to catch non-compliance.
